blocks.heading: Evaluate protection through its effects
blocks.text: A protection measure should address a specified risk and be practical to implement. Compare its worker benefits, employer adjustments, public resources and possible unintended effects. A minimum-pay rule can improve earnings for covered workers paid below it, while increasing their employer’s wage cost if it applies and is enforced. A safety condition can prevent avoidable harm and disruption but needs equipment, instruction and checking. Cost alone does not show a measure should be abandoned; identify whether a proportionate implementation can preserve protection. Do not assume a rule guarantees compliance or that every employer responds by cutting jobs.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: A safety standard requires Nela Goods to guard an exposed machine. A suitable effective guard is available and the cost is manageable. The guard directly addresses the stated hazard, while instruction and checks help it work. Prefer implementation with monitoring to ignoring the risk. A leaflet alone would not physically guard the machine, even if it improves awareness.
